utterances.text: Now, I was not going to ask this witness how he identified his son. As far as I'm aware, there is no dispute that his son was exhumed at Ovcara. I'm quite prepared to do it if my learned friends wish to contest it, but for my part I'm not aware that there will be any contesting of this particular matter. It is sensitive to this witness, and I don't wish to do it unless absolutely necessary. Could I have some indications, please, if there's any dispute here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We absolutely agree with the approach of the Prosecutor, and then we are going to consult during the break and then we will give you our positions. Now it's about close to the break, so we would just like to have a little bit of time so that we can consult on this amongst ourselves and then we will state our position after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Moore, you can continue on the basis that for the moment at least there is no dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: At the moment I have no further questions. I was going to conclude with that particular topic at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much, Mr. Moore. Mr. Vasic -- Mr. Domazet. The pillar isn't getting any slimmer. I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- it continues to hide you completely from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm ready to start with the cross-examination, but I would personally rather have the break now because of the consultations that my colleague Mr. Lukic mentioned also. And I think that then after the break I will require the whole session for my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Domazet. There are redactions, so the break will be for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Domazet, has there been any conclusion reached about the matter raised just before the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have agreed with what our learned friend, Mr. Moore, has said and we believe there is no need for cross-examination on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. I thank you and all Defence counsel. We can proceed on the basis that the -- that matter is not in dispute. Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I am Vladimir Domazet, and I am the co-counsel of Mr. Mrksic. I will be asking you questions on behalf of Mr. Mrksic's defence. First a few questions on your career.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move in to private session so that nothing is made public that could reveal your identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about the period of 1990 and early 1991. As you've described it yourself, it was a period where you as a long-time citizen of Vukovar, you had lived there for 30 years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The year 1990, I'm sure you remember it by the events that were going on in the former Yugoslavia at the time and that was the creation of the multi-party system and the first multi-party elections. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How did the results of the first multi-party elections in Croatia reflect on the situation in Vukovar itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: For people of Serb ethnicity, I believe that it reflected negatively. And as for the Croat people, I think it was reflected positively.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say that, sir, that for people of Serb ethnicity you believe that it was a negative reflection, why do you say that? Why did you form that opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think that those people spontaneously came out into the streets and they protested the results of those elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The results of the elections in Croatia were actually the victory of the HDZ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the local elections in Vukovar? How did they proceed in this multi-party system for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think that the HDZ party also won in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember who was elected president of the Municipal Assembly of Vukovar then, following the local elections?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think that it was the late Mr. Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember or do you know which party he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Well, I can guess. I think that he was in the SDP party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that a party headed by Mr. Racan, at one time a very prominent member of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia and a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And that party, Racan's party, according to what you know, was that a multi-ethnic party, comprising Serbs and Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At the time, and I'm only speaking about that period, did the Serbs have their own national party in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think that in Vukovar they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know how long Mr. Dokmanovic, you remember that he was the president of the Municipal Assembly, how long did he stay as president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think it was until the end -- until the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know why he stopped performing that function?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you recall that at some point before the war broke out, there was an administration imposed? Was there some other type of authority imposed other than the regular authority? Was there any kind of commissioner appointed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: From what you said in your answers to the questions by my learned friend from the Prosecution, it was clear that you know Marin Vidic, Bili. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know what duties he was performing at that time just before the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I think that he was the one who followed after Mr. Dokmanovic. He took over his duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You will probably agree with me and many before you have said the same, that Vukovar and its environs were a national -- a multi-ethnic community. There were not only Croats and Serbs but other ethnic groups as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There were members of 22 ethnic groups living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that a lot of ethnic Serbs lived in Vukovar itself as well as in surrounding areas where they constituted either a majority or wholly populated those areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Is it true that in early 1991, following these elections and after the constitutional changes in the Republic of Croatia, tensions began to emerge in these relations between Serbs and Croats, first of all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you aware that the constitution that I mention which was adopted in late 1990 changed the previous constitution, whereby Serbs as an ethnic group or a nation no longer constituted an integral part of the Republic of Croatia, but it was formulated in the following way, that Croats were members of the Republic of Croatia and that this was, in a way, something that created the initial concerns by Serbs living in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Today you mention the tragic incident in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, but what I'm interested in is a little bit before that because when you spoke about that event you talked about the roadblocks and barricades. Could you tell us actually what was beginning to happen before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Before that I said that ethnic Serbs, as you said, those who lived in the villages where they constituted a majority, set up barricades in -- at the entrances to their village because -- actually, I don't know what the reason was for this, but it was probably partly done out of fear because of what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were any such barricades set up in predominantly Croat areas and settlements, such as Borovo Naselje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: There was a barricade set up between Borovo Naselje and Borovo Selo near the railway track. I know about that one. The only barricade that was set up was near the village of Sotin, which was the only predominantly Croat village in the surroundings of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Although at the time you were no longer working, do you perhaps happen to know, based on conversations that you had with your friends, that a number of Serbs no longer reported for work in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke about what happened in Borovo Selo on the 2nd of May, 1991, you said that this incident, for you, marked the beginning of clashes. Can you tell me what specifically was going on in Vukovar in May and June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I can't be certain. I don't know what preceded the police being dispatched to Borovo Selo, to begin with. At this point in time, Vukovar's police was still a regular institution, and they were free to move about all of Vukovar's different areas, including Borovo Selo. But we all know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, but I wasn't asking about the details of that particular incident. I assume you don't know that much about it. What I was asking is how this affected whatever happened in Vukovar in May and June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: This was a signal for people in Vukovar to start organising themselves. They all believed, as I did myself, that this was not the end of it, that this was no isolated incident, but rather a massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What specific steps were taken? You mentioned preparations of some kind. What exactly did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: People started organising for the town's defence. People started obtaining weapons and, as I say, they were organising the town's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say "the town's defence," preparing the town's defence, what sort of preparation do you have in mind specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: They started setting up small groups of people in certain areas in Vukovar such as Mitnica, Borovo Naselje, Luzac, and such-like. People started setting up units for the town's defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The setting up of these defence units and organising people, did this entail obtaining weapons for these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: It probably did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you please tell me if earlier on, perhaps in the spring of that year, you heard anything about unarmed units being reviewed under the aegis of the HDZ in a number of villages around Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I am not aware of anything like that happening in Vukovar itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I didn't mean Vukovar itself, but what about villages such as Bogdanovci, Lovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I heard something about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HDZ? I suppose not, but please correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I was not a member of the HDZ or any party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: That was my understanding after that answer that you just provided, but I need to ask all the same because I believe these reviews that I am talking about had been organised by the HDZ, of all parties. So you heard people talk about this but you don't know anything more about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear anything about people finding different other ways of purchasing and obtaining weapons in their own time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes. That was also something that started happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know when the Crisis Staff was established in Vukovar itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Roughly speaking in relation to the incident at Borovo Selo, how soon after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I think quite soon after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you personally hear from anyone about explosions, fires in catering establishments and private homes during the spring and early summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: There was this one time that I saw something, but other than that I heard about things happening, just like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Based on any conversations that you had with people about this, was this another factor which contributed to the growing sense of disquiet among the residents of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I should think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mentioned August as the period when armed clashes began. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I suppose you know where the JNA barracks was located in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell me if the JNA were facing any problems entering or leaving the barracks or travelling around the Vukovar area at all, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that columns of vehicles were stopped in certain places because of check-points or barricades set up by the civilian population or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: What about the barracks itself, was it not under siege at one point because its water, electricity supplies, as well as phone lines were cut off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Throughout this period of time, I mean until the end of November, were the JNA people leaving the barracks throughout this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Today in answer to one of the questions asked by my learned friend, you used that map of Vukovar to mark the front line, the confrontation line, or whatever I should call it. You remember that, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If necessary, we can show the map again for you to have a look. But would you agree with me, sir, if I said that at this point in time the JNA barracks found itself behind the front line in a way, isolated, and surrounded by the defending forces, as you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know when this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would it be of any assistance to you if we tried showing you the map again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No, I don't think that's necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Fair enough. You say that the line stayed like that for quite some time and that the only major shift occurred when the withdrawal occurred, which you marked in that other drawing that you made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you give us an idea when this happened exactly and how long it took, some sort of a time-line, please, of this shift between the two lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: That was in early September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "early September," what are we talking about? The first line being established or the second line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: That was after the barracks had been taken and the second line was been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You say after the barracks had been taken. By whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: The line moved from the barracks closer to the town centre once the JNA had entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that before this time there was no communication between the JNA forces inside the barracks and the JNA forces outside the barracks or at the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Can you ask that question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that the JNA barracks was entirely surrounded and besieged by the Croatian forces until the other front line was eventually established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You yourself said that the barracks was taken when the second front line was established and that it was at this point in time that the JNA reached the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I may have misspoken, but the barracks was never in anybody else's hands but the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I agree with you fully on that one. It definitely wasn't, but there was this one point in time when the barracks found itself behind or within the lines occupied by the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have please Exhibit 185, Mr. Usher. I would like to show the witness this exhibit. It was just admitted today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you see this, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You explained today about the line that you marked with the letter A. That was the front line or the first front line, if I may call it that, up until a certain point in time. You see just behind that line, on the inside of that line, as it were, the mark for the JNA barracks. This seems to imply that the barracks was located in an area controlled by the Croatian forces. I do agree that the JNA never left the barracks, but throughout this period of time the JNA barracks was in an area where it was surrounded by Croat defenders. Would you agree with me, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can take the exhibit off now. But next I would like to show Exhibit 186.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You remember this one, sir, don't you? You drew a line today and explained that the second front line, as it were, was near Sajmiste. If we look at this, it's clear that the JNA's outside. What I want to know is about the positions at Mitnica, positions that were still under the control of the forces. You agree with me, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: That's at Mitnica between Vucedol and the first houses in Mitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you mark that for us on this map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We intend to tender this as a separate exhibit. We don't want to spoil this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I assume this is the continuation of that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Maybe it's easier for us to have a clean map, a new one. Do you want a fresh, unmarked map, or do you want a new one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please take this exhibit off then and place -- and place 186 -- 156. I see that the transcript suggests 186. I meant 156.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you now find your way around, sir? The JNA barracks, you see that, right? The front line at Mitnica, can you mark that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. Don't zoom in too much because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between Vucedol and Mitnica. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you draw a line towards Luzac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could please zoom out a little so that we can see Luzac to see if the witness can ... Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Could you please put a letter A where Mitnica is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you see Luzac on this map, sir? Mark it with a letter B, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This map will be assigned exhibit number 189, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Sir, now I'd like to go back to August 1991. You mentioned that the first shelling of Vukovar occurred in August, and planes flying over. I think you personally saw these planes, if I'm not mistaken. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Those two planes that you were talking about, do you know that those were actually shot down while flying over Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Have you ever heard anything about those two planes being shot down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "no," you mean you didn't hear anything about it at the time, you didn't know about it at the time? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you tell me when you found out and what you found out about these airplanes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: From stories of some people. I found out that the planes were shot down at the other side of town. I didn't see it. People talked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know when in August this happened? When did you see these planes, since you didn't see them being shot down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I saw them in early August.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Are you sure about that, sir, since many have already said that this happened sometime -- approximately on the 24th of August when the planes appeared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Well, perhaps they saw other planes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me what your role was in the war. Were you mobilised? In what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I wasn't mobilised. I was a member of the civilian protection of the town of Vukovar. You all know what the tasks of civilian protection are: Taking care of the civilian population, provision of food, water, medicines, and everything else that is implied by the work of members of the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When did you start doing this work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Sometime after I moved from my own building to the shelter opposite from the hospital at the -- the shelter at the Vupik building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you spoke before about preparations, you also talked about May and June after the incident in Borovo Selo. You said that preparations started in food, weapons, and so on. You didn't participate in that, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, at that time you were 43 years old or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that as you were a reserve officer, a trained reserve officer, and then you also knew a lot from your earlier jobs, how is it possible that you were not mobilised into the Croatian forces which surely didn't have that many people at its disposal, in view of your training in the military skills?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I was an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So that's why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So does that mean that even before that you were not obliged to serve in the military. You were excused from serving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I was excused and I was no longer summoned to perform any task.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: If I understand you properly, if you are exempt from military service, then you were not called up. That was your case, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you ever officially ask that a medical commission establish the degree of your disability?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I asked for that before the conflict broke out. I asked to be exempt. I asked the military department to exempt me, but after that I no longer made such a request.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you replied to questions by my learned friend about the public wells in Vukovar, you said that there were many such wells. My question is about the private wells. Am I correct when I say that each private home in Vukovar or practically every private house in Vukovar had its own well that provided water but not drinking water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I don't think that that is correct. It wasn't possible to dig so many wells. The ones that did operate were used. It depends on the owner. They were used for whatever their owner saw fit to use them for.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Since Vukovar is on the banks of the Danube, that water is not at a large depth, so it is easy to get to that water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: If I may correct you, the wells in Vukovar drew their water from the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. I won't insist on that, but ... You mentioned that from the time you left your apartment you -- you went to the shelter which was close to the military and police buildings in Vukovar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you said that you were there until the 15th of November. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You also said today that on at least two occasions or on two occasions you saw Dr. Vesna Bosanac and Mr. Marin Bili in the shelter, and their visits related to the negotiations that were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That was on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So it's logical that this happened before the 15th. Can you determine how much before the 15th you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: It was probably 10 or 15 days before the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who they had these negotiations with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: They said that they conducted talks with representatives of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you know that on the basis of what they said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before I continue with my questions I would like to clarify something in the transcript. It states the 15th, but it does not say the 15th of November. We're speaking about November. When we talked about the 15th, what we meant was the 15th of November. Thank you. You mentioned two occasions. What was the first time that you saw them and what was the second time, and how much time passed between those two occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: The two occasions were about two or three days apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: So you saw them twice within a period of three days. And on both occasions it was said that they were discussing evacuation with representatives of the JNA, evacuation from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Before we go on, unfortunately we still have a problem with the transcript. I think that you confirmed something but it wasn't recorded in the transcript, that this is November, that it is the 15th of November, that it's that date, that we are talking about that month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise, but I had to say it again because of the transcript. After that, during those few days, you said the first meeting was ten days before and then the second one was a couple of days after that. Did you hear from somebody else perhaps, if not from them, what was going on with these talks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And on the 15th of November did you hear anything? Was that the reason why you moved into the hospital or --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: I mentioned that there was talk about negotiations being conducted between the JNA and Vukovar city representatives. We were not 100 per cent informed about the negotiations, so out of caution I decided to go to the hospital with my wife because I thought that if anything were to happen a larger crowd is more powerful, and there are more or better possibilities to stay alive in a bigger crowd. So that was the main reason why I moved to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that today you mentioned how you heard that the fall of Vukovar was inevitable, that it was bound to happen, and perhaps that was also one of the reasons why you moved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Because I was in the centre of town, in the middle of the events close to the MUP, they were with us, from what they said I heard that there were no longer any resources left for defence, that the hospital was packed with wounded, not only the hospital but other shelters as well, and that was one of the reasons for going to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. That day you came to the hospital with your wife. Where did you stay at the hospital? Did anybody approve that you stayed there, if you sought anybody's approval?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Well, we didn't seek anyone's approval. We settled in a corner somewhere. We thought that was the safest place. It was in the basement of the hospital, which was packed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in the hall on the ground floor of the hospital because the basement was so packed and there was no room for anyone else, and also the atmosphere there was terrible, so that's why we found a place for ourselves in the hall of the hospital, believing that that was the safest place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Were you also together with people who were sick or wounded or were they placed somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: They were in the basement of the hospital. We were above in the hall of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: At that time there still weren't that many civilians at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Right when we came, there weren't too many civilians from other shelters that were near the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And you stayed there. Neither you or your wife left the hospital until the 19th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P-007
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm finished with one topic, and I think it's time to complete our work for today. I plan to continue and also finish tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, thank you. Yes, well, there's only a minute to go so there's little point on turning to a new topic. We must adjourn now for the day, as another trial continues shortly. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
